correctness.rationale: For positive entries and exactly three firms and workers, complete EF1 forces three singleton bundles, and conversely singleton bundles are EF1. The financing inequalities suffice: assign each deviating worker to a best firm in the coalition and sum that firm's deviation surplus covered by its profit. The high-edge maximum matching gives one, two or three high assignments; size one forces one common high firm, and size two forces the unfilled pair to be low. Substituting the specified normalized wages into the surplus bounds gives respectively (1+2δ)/3, at least (1+δ)/2, and one. The common-high instance has EF1 welfare 1+2δ versus unrestricted welfare three, and the grand coalition bounds the factor. At δ=1 the actual high graph is complete, the frontier is one, and subcases for noncomplete labeled graphs merely duplicate the same valuation matrix in the finite tests. An independent exact-rational reproduction checked EF1, financing and all 56 coalition inequalities for each of 1,715 certificates; matched-size counts 3, 93, 247. That replay does not replace the continuum argument.
